q: A company wants a customer chatbot that can check order status, process returns and answer FAQ questions. Which combination fits?
o: A Bedrock agent with action groups for the order APIs and a knowledge base for FAQs
Amazon Polly with a static FAQ page
A regression model on order totals
e: Agents handle actions through APIs, and knowledge bases supply FAQ facts. Together they cover both needs.

q: Which pairs a generative AI use case with a sensible design choice? (Choose TWO.)
o: Answering from frequently updated manuals: RAG
Matching a strict house writing style: fine-tuning or detailed few-shot prompts
Real-time facts: continued pre-training once a year
e: RAG suits fresh facts. Fine-tuning or strong prompts suit consistent style. Exact or high-stakes outputs need deterministic logic and human oversight.

q: What should you do first when a prompt gives inconsistent results?
o: Make the instructions clearer and more specific, and add examples
e: Prompt refinement is the cheapest fix. Only escalate to RAG or fine-tuning if prompting can't reach the bar.

q: Which output format request is most reliable for an app that must parse the model's reply?
o: Ask for a strict JSON object with named fields, and validate it in code
Ask for a numbered list with emojis
e: Structured output (JSON with a schema) plus validation makes replies machine-readable and safe to parse.
an: RPGACE asks Oracle for a RECIPE_JSON trailer, then parses it defensively. It even handles code fences the model wraps around it.

q: Why should an application validate model output in code rather than trust it directly?
o: Models can produce malformed or unsafe output even with a good prompt
e: Defensive parsing and sanitising protect your app and data from bad or manipulated outputs.
an: RPGACE's _sanitizeNewSteps strips odd names from AI-suggested taxonomy steps, so a bad reply can't corrupt the tree.

q: What is the main benefit of returning the first part of a long AI job immediately and finishing the rest in the background?
o: Users see results quickly instead of waiting for the whole batch
It reduces token cost to zero
It removes the need for storage
e: Streaming or progressive results improve the user experience for long generations.
an: Bookworm used to take about 7 minutes before showing anything. Now it shows the first insight right away and fills in the rest in the background.

q: What is a key consideration when choosing an embedding model for RAG?
o: It should handle your language and content type, and must be the same model used for both documents and queries
It must be the largest image model available
It must use the highest temperature
It must be trained by your company
e: Queries and documents must be embedded with the same model so the vectors are comparable. Language and domain fit matter.

q: A support team wants answers drawn from both a knowledge base and live order data. Which design is most suitable?
o: An agent that queries the knowledge base and calls the order API as a tool
e: Live data needs tool calls at answer time. Static knowledge comes from retrieval.

q: Why might a company choose Amazon Q Business instead of building its own RAG app?
o: It is a managed assistant that connects to company data sources with existing permissions, with little building required
It gives full control over model weights
It requires no data at all
e: Q Business is a ready-made enterprise assistant. Building your own with Bedrock gives more control but needs more work.

q: Which is the best first step to evaluate whether a summarisation model is good enough?
o: Test it on a representative set of your own documents and compare with reference summaries and human review
Read the provider's marketing page only
Use it in production and wait for complaints
e: Evaluate on your own data with the right metrics (such as ROUGE) plus human judgement before deploying.

q: Which risk increases when an AI agent can browse the web and act on what it reads?
o: Indirect prompt injection from malicious web content
e: Agents reading external content can be manipulated by hidden instructions in it. Separate data from instructions and restrict tools.

q: Which describes the term 'temperature 0' in practice?
o: The model nearly always picks the most likely next token, giving very consistent output
e: Temperature near zero makes output close to deterministic. Good for extraction and classification.

q: Which customisation keeps the model unchanged and is the fastest to try?
e: Prompt engineering needs no training and can be changed instantly.

q: What is the role of a guardrail in a RAG chatbot? (Choose TWO.)
o: Block harmful or off-topic requests and responses
Check answers are grounded in the retrieved sources
e: Bedrock Guardrails filter content, deny topics, redact personal data and run contextual grounding checks.

q: A company's AI feature must work even if the model provider is unavailable. Which design helps?
o: A fallback path, such as a queue to process later or a simpler backup response
e: Resilient AI apps degrade gracefully: queue, retry with backoff, or switch to a fallback.

q: Which signals that RAG, not fine-tuning, is the better fit?
o: The answers must cite sources and the data changes often
The model must adopt a fixed brand tone
Latency must be as low as possible with no retrieval
e: Citations and fresh data point to RAG. Style and behaviour point to fine-tuning.

q: Which is an example of a tool an agent might call?
o: A weather API that returns today's forecast
e: Tools are external functions or APIs (search, databases, calculators) that agents use to act or fetch facts.

q: Which consideration matters most when a generative AI app serves users in many languages?
o: Choosing a model with strong multilingual support
e: Language coverage varies between models. Evaluate in each target language.

q: An app must keep conversation history across turns. What is the simplest way with a stateless model API?
o: Send the relevant previous messages along with each new request
e: Model APIs are stateless. The app supplies the history (or a summary of it) each turn, within the context window.

q: Which practice controls cost in a high-volume generative AI app? (Choose TWO.)
o: Use the smallest model that meets quality
Cap max tokens and keep prompts concise
Send the full document every time
e: Right-size the model, trim prompts, cap outputs, cache repeated prefixes and use batch for offline work.
an: RPGACE's token rules: cheap keyword filter first, skip the AI call if nothing matches, never send full path listings, and use the cheap model for mechanical work.

q: What does 'chunk overlap' mean in RAG indexing?
o: Adjacent chunks share some text, so ideas split at a boundary aren't lost
Two copies of the model run together
e: Overlap keeps context that straddles chunk boundaries.

q: Which describes a knowledge base's 'metadata filtering'?
o: Restricting retrieval to chunks with certain attributes, such as department or date
e: Metadata filters make retrieval more precise and can enforce simple access rules.

q: Which outcome shows a fine-tuning job was worthwhile?
o: The tuned model beats the base model plus good prompting on your evaluation set, at acceptable cost
e: Always compare against a strong baseline (prompting or RAG). Fine-tuning must earn its cost.

q: Which describes Amazon Bedrock's Converse API?
o: One consistent API for multi-turn conversations that works across supported models
e: Converse gives a single message format for chat and tool use across Bedrock models, so switching models is easier.

q: An app needs the model to call a function to get a stock price before answering. What capability is this?
e: With tool use, the model asks the app to run a defined function and uses the result in its answer.

q: Which helps evaluate a RAG system specifically? (Choose TWO.)
o: Whether the right chunks were retrieved (retrieval quality)
Whether the answer is faithful to the retrieved text
The colour scheme of the app
e: Measure retrieval (relevance and recall of chunks) and generation (faithfulness, correctness). Bedrock evaluations support RAG metrics.

q: A business wants a quick prototype to show executives a generative AI idea with no code. Which is the best fit?
o: PartyRock (Amazon Bedrock Playground) or the Bedrock console playground
e: Playgrounds give fast, no-code prototypes before investing in a build.

q: Why test prompts with real, representative user inputs before launch?
o: Real inputs reveal failures that tidy test examples miss
e: Real-world inputs are messier. Representative testing catches edge cases and formatting breaks.
an: RPGACE found its numbered-list bug only on a real screenshot: Oracle's lists lost their numbers in the chat display, so features now ask for a single ' | ' line instead.
